svg.text: Six ways every system gets attacked — and the Azure controls that shut each one down.
SUBJECT: ANY SYSTEM WITH USERS, DATA, OR A NETWORK
Run the drill: for every component, ask six questions
Draw your data-flow diagram, mark trust boundaries, then walk S-T-R-I-D-E across every element that crosses one.
Can someone pretend to be a user, service, or server?
Entra ID + phishing-resistant MFA · managed identities · certificate-bound tokens
Can data or code be modified in transit, at rest, or in the pipeline?
TLS everywhere · immutable blob storage · code signing · Key Vault + HSM keys
Can an actor deny an action because you can't prove it happened?
Entra + activity audit logs · Azure Monitor · Microsoft Sentinel with immutable retention
Can data leak to anyone not authorized to see it?
Encryption at rest & in transit · Private Link · Microsoft Purview labels & DLP
Can the system be degraded or knocked offline?
Azure DDoS Protection · Front Door + WAF · autoscale · rate limiting & quotas
Can a low-privilege identity gain rights it was never granted?
Azure RBAC least privilege · PIM just-in-time · Defender for Cloud attack-path analysis
Threat modeling is a habit, not a document. Re-run STRIDE every time the architecture changes.
The Visual Playbook Series — cloud security, taught like it should be.
